rights: You have the right to receive salary for all days worked.
Your employer cannot withhold earned wages without a lawful reason.
You can ask for written salary records and deduction details.
You can complain to the Labour Department if salary is delayed.
law: Shops and Establishments Act of the relevant State
steps: Send a written email or letter to HR asking for pending salary with dates.
Keep a copy of all messages, payslips, attendance records, and bank statements.
If there is no response, send a legal notice through a lawyer or labour union.
File a complaint with the local Labour Commissioner or Labour Department.
documents: Attendance records, emails, or chat proof

rights: You have the right to notice or salary in lieu of notice if your contract provides it.
You can ask for the termination reason in writing.
Termination cannot be illegal, discriminatory, or against service rules.
Eligible workmen can raise an industrial dispute.
law: Shops and Establishments Act of the relevant State
steps: Read your appointment letter and company policy for notice rules.
Ask HR for written reasons and final settlement details.
Send a written representation requesting reinstatement or compensation.
Approach the Labour Department or Labour Court if the dispute continues.

rights: You have the right to wages for overtime work where the law applies.
Employers must follow legal working-hour limits.
You can ask for records of attendance and overtime.
You can complain if overtime is forced or unpaid.
law: Shops and Establishments Act of the relevant State
steps: Prepare a date-wise list of extra hours worked.
Ask HR or accounts for overtime payment in writing.
Collect shift rosters, biometric logs, emails, and manager instructions.
File a complaint with the Labour Inspector if payment is denied.
documents: Emails or chats assigning extra work

rights: Eligible employees have the right to provident fund and ESI benefits.
Deductions from salary must be deposited with the relevant authority.
You can check contributions using your UAN or ESI number.
You can complain if deductions are made but not deposited.
law: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
steps: Check your EPFO passbook or ESI portal for contribution entries.
Ask HR for UAN, ESI number, and contribution proof.
Raise a grievance on the EPFO or ESIC portal.
Complain to the regional PF or ESI office if the employer does not respond.

rights: A landlord generally cannot evict you without due legal process.
You have the right to peaceful possession during the tenancy.
Basic utilities cannot be cut to force you to leave.
You can seek police help or court protection against forceful eviction.
law: Rent Control Act of the relevant State
steps: Check your rent agreement for notice period and termination clause.
Reply in writing if the landlord is forcing you to vacate.
Do not sign any blank or forced document.
Approach police or civil court if there is threat, lockout, or utility disconnection.
documents: Rent receipts or bank transfer proof

rights: You can claim return of security deposit after lawful deductions.
The landlord should explain deductions with proof.
Normal wear and tear should not be treated as damage.
You can recover deposit through legal notice or civil proceedings.
law: Rent Control Act of the relevant State
steps: Send a written demand for refund with bank details.
Ask for a break-up of deductions and repair bills.
Share move-out photos showing property condition.
Send a legal notice and approach the Rent Authority or civil court if needed.

rights: You have the right to peaceful enjoyment of the rented property.
The landlord cannot enter without reasonable permission.
Threats, abuse, utility cuts, or lockouts can be challenged.
You can seek police help for intimidation or unlawful entry.
law: Rent Control Act of the relevant State
steps: Keep a dated record of harassment incidents.
Send a written warning asking the landlord to stop unlawful conduct.
Call police if there is threat, violence, lockout, or utility disconnection.
Seek an injunction from civil court for repeated harassment.

rights: Rent increases must follow the rent agreement or applicable rent law.
You can dispute sudden or unfair rent hikes.
You have the right to receipts for rent paid.
You can approach the Rent Authority where available.
law: Rent Control Act of the relevant State
steps: Check the rent escalation clause in your agreement.
Ask the landlord to give the rent increase demand in writing.
Continue paying agreed rent through traceable mode.
Approach the Rent Authority or civil court if the increase is unlawful.

rights: You have the right to receive safe and defect-free goods.
You can ask for repair, replacement, refund, or compensation.
Misleading product claims can be challenged.
You can file a consumer complaint if the seller refuses relief.
steps: Contact the seller or brand customer care immediately.
Record the defect with photos or videos.
Send a written complaint asking for refund, repair, or replacement.
File a complaint on National Consumer Helpline or Consumer Commission.

rights: You can claim refund if the seller failed to deliver goods or services.
Refund terms must be clear and not unfair.
E-commerce platforms must provide grievance redressal.
You can claim compensation for unfair trade practice.
steps: Raise a refund request through the seller or platform in writing.
Keep order ID, ticket number, and refund timeline proof.
Escalate to the platform grievance officer.
File a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline or Consumer Commission.
documents: Emails or chat with customer support

rights: You have the right to services performed with reasonable care.
You can claim refund or compensation for deficient service.
You can complain against delay, negligence, or refusal after payment.
You can approach the Consumer Commission for relief.
steps: Send a written complaint to the service provider.
Ask for refund, completion of service, or compensation.
Keep proof of payment and service promise.
File a consumer complaint if the provider does not respond.
documents: Photos or proof of poor service

rights: You can claim warranty service during the valid warranty period.
The company cannot deny genuine warranty without a valid reason.
You can ask for repair, replacement, or refund depending on the defect.
Repeated failed repairs may support a consumer complaint.
steps: Visit an authorized service center and ask for a job sheet.
Request the denial reason in writing.
Escalate to the brand grievance officer.
File a consumer complaint if warranty is wrongly refused.
